title: Valid Triangle Number
statement: Count the triples of positions `i < j < k` in `nums` whose three values could be the side lengths of a real triangle, meaning each value is strictly less than the sum of the other two. Triples are counted by position, so equal values at different indices form different triples. Return the count.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every triple against all three triangle inequalities is O(n³). Sorting removes most of that work: if `a <= b <= c`, the triple is a triangle exactly when `a + b > c`, because the other two inequalities hold automatically. So fix the largest side `nums[k]` and count pairs to its left whose sum beats it. In a sorted range that count can be done with two pointers: when the smallest and largest candidates already beat `nums[k]`, every value between them works too.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order and set `count = 0`.
2. For each `k` from the last index down to 2, treat `nums[k]` as the longest side.
3. Put `left` at index 0 and `right` at `k - 1`.
4. If `nums[left] + nums[right] > nums[k]`, then every index from `left` to `right - 1` pairs with `right`, so add `right - left` and move `right` down.
5. Otherwise `nums[left]` is too small for any remaining partner, so move `left` up.
6. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted, `nums` is `[2, 2, 3, 4]`. With `k = 3` (side 4): `left = 0`, `right = 2`, and `2 + 3 > 4`, so both 2s pair with the 3: `count = 2`, `right = 1`. Now `2 + 2 > 4` fails, so `left = 1` and the loop ends. With `k = 2` (side 3): `2 + 2 > 3`, adding `1`. The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): the sort is O(n log n), and for each `k` the pointers meet after at most `k` steps.
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the in-place sort.

## Pitfalls

- The inequality is strict: `1, 2, 3` is flat, not a triangle, so use `>` rather than `>=`.
- Zeros can never be a side; the strict test already rejects them, so no special case is needed.
- Add `right - left` pairs at once, not just 1, or most valid triples are missed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | number of valid triples found so far |
| `k` | index of the longest side in the sorted array |
| `left`, `right` | the two pointers over indices `0..k-1` |

narration.2: Sort so that the last value of a triple is its longest side.
narration.4: Try each index k as the longest side, from the end down to the third element.
narration.5: left starts at the smallest value...
narration.6: ...and right at the largest value below nums[k].
narration.7: Keep going until the pointers meet.
narration.8: With a sorted triple, beating the longest side is the only check needed.
narration.9: Every index from left to right - 1 also pairs with right, so add them all.
narration.10: right has been paired with every useful partner; move it down.
narration.12: nums[left] is too small even with the largest partner, so move left up.
narration.16: All pairs for every longest side have been counted.
